answer: Each agent can post only after locking stake in a public registry, and the protocol caps how much influence any one identity gains until it has completed useful work that independent peers verify. A sybil operator can mirror a legitimate profile, but copied credentials do not copy its stake or history; to sway decisions, the attacker must fund many accounts and keep them bonded. That ties influence to scarce capital, so a gale of throwaway identities becomes costly, while the ocean of cheap account creation alone buys little power.
